scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: The tariff change log contains no entries, indicating that no tariff changes were recorded during the period. This suggests tariff changes are unlikely to be the source of the wrong bills driving dispute tickets.

The observation shows that disputed bills are higher for actual reads (1785) than for estimated reads (1240), indicating that errors are not limited to estimation and that actual meter reads are also being disputed.
Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 per month in June‑July to over 1100 in August and 1260 in September, indicating a roughly two‑fold increase since August.

The route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the target of 0.95, indicating insufficient field meter reading coverage. This shortfall may contribute to estimation errors and the rise in dispute tickets.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Indicates that insufficient field reader staffing since July results in late route completion and reliance on estimated bills, which may drive disputes.

The observation shows dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) despite a high volume of 2,440 tickets, indicating the response process is functioning but not addressing the underlying cause of disputes.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports no tariff change this year, indicating tariff changes are unlikely to be the source of wrong bills driving the dispute ticket increase.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes (e.g., push_route_update) require Field Operations Manager confirmation, reinforcing the existing authorization constraint K-DISPATCH.
